posts.headline: This City Mushroom Farm Grows Fungi For Chicago's Top Chefs — And 'The Bear'
posts.blurb: The mushrooms Carmy plates on The Bear are real, and they grow indoors in a West Loop warehouse. Four Star supplies a lot of Chicago's best kitchens from a building most people walk past.
posts.why: Hidden-in-plain-sight Chicago address doing something unexpected — the exact shape of a good route stop.

posts.headline: How renaming one Philly street sets the precedent for change
posts.blurb: Taney Street became LeCount Street in 2024: thirty blocks of Philadelphia renamed for a 19th-century teacher who refused to give up her streetcar seat. It took the neighborhood six years.
posts.why: Street names as a way to read a city's history — how we want players looking at Philadelphia.

posts.headline: Toronto Blue Jays players go on Tim Hortons coffee run in full gear
posts.blurb: Two Blue Jays walked into a Toronto Tim Hortons in full game gear and ordered eight double-doubles, two dozen donuts and 50 timbits. The team coffee run is apparently a real assignment.
posts.why: Team ritual crossed with a city institution — the stadium-culture overlap our games live in.

posts.headline: Anatomy of a Cleveland classic — The Polish Boy
posts.blurb: Kielbasa, fries, slaw and barbecue sauce, all in one bun. A Cleveland comic artist diagrams the Polish Boy and the decades-old argument over who makes it properly.
posts.why: A whole city's pride packed into one sandwich, and a natural Cleveland stop.

posts.headline: NBA championship trophy on display at Natural History Museum
posts.blurb: The Knicks championship trophy is parked in the American Museum of Natural History's gem and mineral hall until January, a few cases from one of Jesse Owens' 1936 gold medals.
posts.why: An odd juxtaposition hiding inside a landmark New York building — memorable stop material.
